# Alexandria Configuration

**Generated by:** Alexandria Initialize v1.0
**Date:** 2026-04-22
**Configuration:** Factory × Low Novelty × Low Complexity
**Pool:** 22 areas — 5 Foundation / 4 Core / 9 Amplifier / 4 Deprioritized

## Your Risk Profile

> **Silent wrong defaults — hundreds of autonomous micro-decisions that cumulatively define the experience.**

Your library is the comprehensive product knowledge graph that autonomous agents need for every decision. At Factory mode, the library carries the load that a live product owner would otherwise carry — when an agent has to decide error-message tone, the shape of the metadata page, or the default retention behavior on deletion, the answer has to be recorded somewhere or it gets re-invented per decision.

## Product Context (from first-session conversation)

`fabro.report` is an intake service for debug bundles produced by the `fabro debug` command in the main [Fabro](../../../fabro) product. A Fabro user with a bug runs `fabro report`, which uploads a compressed tarball to S3 and returns a short URL. The Fabro team (Bryan + team) triages bugs by retrieving bundles directly from S3.

Key product decisions already made:

- **Scope:** upload → S3 → URL. No symbolication, no rendering, no UI beyond a one-page metadata receipt.
- **Template:** `bun.report`'s intake shape, narrowed. Not its downstream processing surface.
- **Security:** capability URLs — possession of the URL grants view + delete. No auth.
- **Retention:** 30 days default.
- **Metadata:** Fabro version captured outside the bundle; optional reporter message; arbitrary key/value tags (no first-class issue link).
- **No content dedup:** bundles expire anyway.
- **Access for Triagers:** direct S3, not through the service.

## Knowledge Areas by Priority

### Foundation — seed first
*Must exist before anything else. Other knowledge depends on them.*

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 1.1 | Product Vision | Vision & Strategy | The library has no anchor. Every card is based on inferences, producing technically accurate but strategically hollow knowledge. |
| 1.2 | Product Strategy | Vision & Strategy | People optimize for different outcomes and don't realize they disagree. |
| 2.2 | Noun Vocabulary | Architecture & Nouns | Two builders working on adjacent features call the same thing by different names. |
| 3.2 | Emotional / Aesthetic Goals | Experience & Feel | The product is functionally correct but emotionally flat. At Factory mode, the tone of error messages, the feel of the receipt page, and defaults get decided by whoever implements them unless this is recorded. |
| 3.5 | Anti-Patterns | Experience & Feel | Builders default to conventions of whatever product category they're most familiar with — for this product, that risk is specifically "drift toward bun.report's full product shape" (symbolication, feedback, rendering) when you explicitly don't want that. |

### Core — seed after Foundation

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 1.4 | Competitive Analysis | Vision & Strategy | Low novelty = many close analogues (bun.report, paste services, support-bundle uploaders). Worth a short writeup of what to borrow and what to skip. |
| 1.5 | Market Requirements | Vision & Strategy | Evidence behind the strategy. Lower pressure at low-novelty but still Core. |
| 4.1 | Design System | Visual & Interaction | For a headless-adjacent service this is light, but Factory-floored — record the receipt-page conventions explicitly so the agent doesn't invent a fresh aesthetic per page. |
| 4.3 | Prototypes / Mockups | Visual & Interaction | A screenshot or sketch of the receipt page is enough; this isn't a heavy area for this product. |

### Amplifier — seed when Foundation + Core are in place

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 1.3 | User Personas / JTBD | Vision & Strategy | Personas are thin here: the Reporter (a Fabro user hitting a bug) and the Triager (Fabro team). Quick JTBD writeup covers both. |
| 2.1 | Information Architecture | Architecture & Nouns | Almost trivial given one entity + one page. Record it so it stays that way. |
| 2.3 | Product Entities | Architecture & Nouns | Partially captured in the discovery section of the config. Needs a proper entity card. |
| 2.4 | System Design | Architecture & Nouns | Invisible mechanisms: retention expiration, bundle storage layout, S3 key scheme. |
| 4.2 | Interaction Patterns | Visual & Interaction | Mostly the CLI's upload UX and the receipt page's delete interaction. Minor. |
| 4.4 | Accessibility Standards | Visual & Interaction | Almost irrelevant for a headless-ish receipt, but named because Factory mode demands a policy somewhere. |
| 5.1 | Key Decisions Log | Decision History | Capability URLs vs auth, no dedup, 30d retention — all of these are decisions worth logging with rationale so the agent doesn't re-litigate them. |
| 5.2+5.4 | Institutional Memory | Decision History | Nothing here yet. Will accumulate. |
| 5.3 | Roadmap | Decision History | Currently "build the intake service." Worth writing down what's explicitly NOT on the roadmap (symbolication, rendering, team dashboards). |

### Deprioritized — seed last, if at all

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 2.5 | Full GDD / PRD | Architecture & Nouns | Product is too small to need a comprehensive spec. The Foundation + Core cards will carry it. |
| 3.1 | User Journey Maps | Experience & Feel | One journey: user runs `fabro report`, gets a URL, pastes it somewhere. Not worth a journey map. |
| 3.3 | Engagement Loops | Experience & Feel | Irrelevant — the product is intentionally used once per bug. |
| 3.4 | Progression / Mastery | Experience & Feel | No progression to design. |

## What This Means

The Factory configuration produces a heavier shape than the product strictly needs — `fabro.report` is a small, bounded, low-novelty service, but because you plan to let agents decide ongoing product behavior autonomously, the library has to record context that a live human would otherwise carry implicitly. The most important Foundation investments are **Product Vision** (anchor), **Noun Vocabulary** (the 5 confirmed entities), and **Anti-Patterns** — the last of which is unusually load-bearing here because the template (`bun.report`) is famously *more* than you want, and without an explicit "this is NOT that" card, an agent with initiative will drift toward it. Design System and Prototypes at Core look heavier than the UI surface justifies; treat those as lightweight captures, not as investments proportional to their tier label.

1. **Source material first.** Sam is drafting initial source material for Product Vision (1.1) from the first-session conversation. Output at `docs/alexandria/sources/product-vision.md`.
2. **Conan review.** Once source material lands, ask Conan to assess it and inventory what cards should be written.
3. **Sam writes cards.** Foundation tier first — Vision (1.1), Strategy (1.2), Noun Vocabulary (2.2), Emotional Goals (3.2), Anti-Patterns (3.5). Anti-Patterns should name the `bun.report` drift risk explicitly.
4. **Iterate.** Conan grades → Sam fixes → repeat.
5. **Move to Core.** Competitive Analysis is the most useful Core card here — a short writeup of what to borrow from `bun.report` and what to skip.
